6. Admitting the above genealogy of the plaintiffs, the defendant contended that Paban Mondal married Sumati alias Subhadra after the death of his first and second wife. When Paban diell Sumati had a daughter, who of course could not live long. So, Paban Mondal died leaving behind, a wife Sumati, and three daughters, namely, Boro Panchi, Jhoharmoni and Choto Panchi. Under the Hindu Dayabagh School of Law, Somatic inherited the suit land as widow and possessed. While she was thus owner in possession, on 29-3-41 one Kali Charan created a fraudulent patta without any salami or consideration to grab the suit land. Sumati ultimately, got back the patta from Kalicharan through litigation up to the Court of District Judge. In the litigations to rescue the suit land, she had to take loan. To repay the loan incurred in litigation, perform the sraddha of her husband and also to maintain her, she had to transfer 10.47 acres of land including the suit land to defendant No. 1 by a registered deed of sale dated 14-5-42 and delivered possession. She also delivered the original copy of the patta to defendant No. 1 along with the sale deed. 

 15. He submits that at the time of alienation on 14-5-42, defendant No. 1 was minor and his father actually did everything on his behalf including taking delivery of possession. All the persons who witnessed the alienation were dead at the time of trial of the suit. In the circumstances, the recitals in the deed exhibit-A in respect of legal necessity for the alienation, the original registered patta Exhibit B dated 29-3-41 and the deeds of gift dated 14-5-52 Exhibit C and C1, if considered together, the legal necessity for the alienation is proved and the Court of appeal below has so found. He concludes, the judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below therefore do not call for any interference. He also cites the authorities in the case of Nanda Lal Dhur Biswas vs Jagat Kishore Acharjya, 36 Indian Cases 420, 29 DLR (SC) 137, AIR 1935 Calcutta 689 and Jagannath and others vs Sreenath and others. (1922) 59 CLJ 167. 

 26. In the case before us, the alience was a minor at the time of alienation. Besides the recitals in the deed Exhibit A, he has got original registered deed of patta created by one Kali Charan, which on the pain of a case he had to return to the widow, Surnati who then delivered it to the alienee and the deeds of gift dated 14-2-56 Exhibit C and CI. We shall see how the Court of appeal below was justified to find that the alienation was proved to be for legal necessity and binds the estate left by Paban Mondal. 

 45. In the absence of direct evidence and on the law as considered above the recitals in the deed deserve consideration as proof of the existence of legal necessity. In support of the necessity to pay off the debt incurred through litigation, the deed of patta is also adduced and marked as exhibit B. The patta shows that an interest was created in respect of the suit land. The interest of Paban Mondal in the land would have been extinguished had the patta been not recovered. Besides, the deeds of gift to Nishikanta and Jhoharmoni Exhibit C and CI also evidence, they including father of the plaintiffs admitted the alienation as valid by accepting the gift and taking possession of their respective land. The conclusion of the Court of appeal below that the alienation by the widow, Sumati to the defendant No. 1 was for legal necessity is therefore well founded, and does not suffer from infirmity or illegality.
